script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 25. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Water is soft.  Rock is hard.  Yet stand at the Grand Canyon and see what water does to stone given enough time.

The Grand Canyon took about 6 million years to carve—one grain at a time. That's roughly 0.01 inches of erosion per year. Invisible progress, year after year, century after century, until: a mile-deep masterpiece. Rivers never flow perfectly straight.  Any tiny irregularity—a rock, a root—redirects flow slightly.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Persistence transforms.  Water isn't strong, but it never stops.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Persistence Inventory - Your Long Carving.

Here's your activity: Identify something you've been working on persistently—a skill, a relationship, a project. Estimate how long you've been at it. Now project forward: what might 5 more years of this patient carving create? Recommit to the slow work. This helps you recognize and commit to long-term shaping forces.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how rivers shape the land can be applied to persistence inventory - your long carving. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
